newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tajiks talk peace in Moscow.
newsitem.headline: Tajiks talk peace in Moscow.

text.p: Peace talks between the Tajik president and the former Soviet republic's armed Islamic opposition started in Moscow on Thursday.

Tajik President Imomali Rakhmonov and the head of the opposition delegation, Sayid Abdullo Nuri, held a working meeting in the evening and full-scale talks were likely to open on Friday, the Russian Foreign Ministry said in a press release.

The discussions, aimed at trying to halt four years of bloody conflict, had initially been scheduled to start in the morning but were postponed until opposition leaders arrived in the Russian capital.
The ministry said the United Nations special envoy to Tajikistan, Gerd Merrem, and Russia's special envoy, Yevgeny Mikhailov, took part in the talks.

RIA news agency quoted a government source in Moscow as saying earlier on Thursday that Russia's Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov would join the talks on Friday.
Rakhmonov seemed in positive mood ahead of Moscow talks.
"The Moscow meeting is fundamental," he told Nezavisimaya Gazeta newspaper in an interview published on Thursday.
"First, we should agree on a full ceasefire and an end to other conflict on the border and within the country for the whole period of the negotiating process."
He said a "reconciliation commission" would work on various political issues including reintegrating the exiled opposition.
"I see no option other than a political settlement by peaceful means. In any event, we are ready for this," he added.
He and Nuri are due to discuss the most recent ceasefire agreement in the war-torn republic. Previous truces have been routinely flouted, sometimes immediately after they were signed.

The latest pact was agreed in talks in Afghanistan, but local officials have already reported fighting between government troops and the opposition in the Garm region, some 150 km (100 miles) east of the capital Dushanbe.

In another incident casting doubt on the viability of the latest truce, United Nations military observers monitoring it were subjected to a mock execution by Tajik government troops, the U.N. mission said on Wednesday.
Opposition sources in Dushanbe said Nuri was delayed in the Iranian capital Tehran for political consultations with other Tajik opposition leaders.
Russian media said Moscow was opposed to Nuri's consultations in Iran and had wanted Nuri to fly direct from Afghanistan to Moscow.
